Ava Chen: Observed p99 spike after we flipped adaptive-kernel for the rlhf models. Was thinking chunk flush interval + microbatch sizing interaction is the culprit.
Diego Ramos: Details? numbers?
Ava Chen:  p95 steady ~220ms, p99 jumped from 480ms -> 1.4s after deploy at 03:12 UTC. CPU/GPU charts show bursts aligned w/ KV cache churn and increased small microbatches.
Priya Kapoor: Hmm could be KV hotset thrash causing kernel switch stutter. Any kernel selection logs from runtime?
Ava Chen: Pasted tail of runtime log below:
```
[03:12:18] kernel-select: chosen=quant-bert-fp16-optimistic latency_est=0.18ms
[03:12:18] kvcache: evict=128 items reason=memory_pressure
[03:12:18] microbatch: size=1->4 ramp=instant
[03:12:18] dispatch: kernel_swap_latency=0.34s
[03:12:19] emit: flush_interval=18ms -> payload_sent=false
[03:12:20] dispatch: retry_on_fallback model_variant=cpu_fallback
```
Diego Ramos: That kernel_swap_latency=0.34s is huge. Might be JITing or CUDA context switch.
Marta Nguyen: We saw similar during last week's canary but didn't see p99 that high. What's different? workload skew or token chunk size?
Ava Chen: Customers hitting streaming mode with chunk_size=16 tokens, flush_interval=18ms. With microbatch reduction, we end up doing more small dispatches each triggering kernel rebinds.
Priya Kapoor: Proposed experiment: 1) increase flush_interval to 40ms 2) cap microbatch min_size=2 3) disable kernel eager-rewrite for that model for 1h canary. Anyone object?
Diego Ramos: +1 on canary. Also capture perf counters: nvtx, cuda-memcp, kernel-id sequence.
Marta Nguyen: Add a tracepoint to record KV cache misses per-request and token offset so we can correlate.
Ava Chen: Creating canary config now. Will tag runtime-bot to run it.
runtime-bot: Canary 2149009999-1 started: redirect 5% traffic to canary pool at 03:45 UTC :rocket:
Diego Ramos: Quick question — if we increase flush_interval, perceived latency might increase for first token. How do we balance p99 vs perceived p10?
Priya Kapoor: Right — tradeoffs: larger flush reduces kernel churn and amortizes overhead but makes initial token wait longer. Measure perceived latency as time-to-first-byte (TTFB) vs completion latency.
Ava Chen: Agreed. We'll capture TTFB, per-token inter-arrival, and p50/p95/p99. Also include subjective human tests for streaming smoothness.
Marta Nguyen: If KV churn is main cause, a short-term mitigation is soft pin popular KV buckets (simple LRU boost) and replay warm RPCs.
Diego Ramos: After canary, if p99 drops but p50 rises slightly, consider adaptive flush: start small for first 2 tokens then expand flush window.
Priya Kapoor: Example pseudo for adaptive flush:
```
if tokens_sent < 2:
  flush_interval = 12ms
else:
  flush_interval = min(40ms, base + tokens_sent*4ms)
```
Ava Chen: Nice. Also adding kernel sticky hint: prefer current kernel for X ms if subsequent requests arrive to same model variant.
runtime-bot: Canary 2149009999-1 completed: p99 pre=1.42s post=0.56s, p50 pre=0.22s post=0.28s, TTFB pre=0.06s post=0.12s. Logs: kv_miss_rate decreased 46%.
Marta Nguyen: That's promising — big p99 improvement with small TTFB regression.
Diego Ramos: Can we run same on a high-concurrency burst (200qps) to see behavior under load? Also collect kernel_swap_latency histogram.
Ava Chen: Scheduling that next. Will also try adaptive flush canary.
Priya Kapoor: Great. Once we have burst numbers, we can pick a default: prefer lower p99 for avg customers, but allow per-customer flush_profile for ultra-low perceived latency.
Marta Nguyen: I'll draft the rollout notes: include toggle flags, monitoring alerts (p99>800ms), and rollback plan.
Ava Chen: Thanks team. I'll share the canary dashboards and the kernel swap traces in this thread.
Diego Ramos: :thumbsup:
